NT1#0.quote: Commonly known as the ‘Lake District’, Nainital is nestled high up in the Kumaon Himalayas at an altitude of around 2,000 m above sea level.

NT2#0.quote: The summer capital of the United Provinces during the British era, the town has a strong colonial heritage with vibrant clusters of villas and bungalows.

NT3#0.quote: Nainital is an all-year destination but the weather is the best between March and June. It receives heavy snowfall in winter and turns into a white wonderland, making it a popular Christmas and New Year destination.

NT4#0.quote: Pantnagar Airport is the nearest airport to Nainital. After that 70 kms distance has to be traveled by road through a bus or cab.

NT5#0.quote: You can reach Kathgodam Railway Station by train and it is 23 km away from Nainital.

NT5#1.quote: A popular Train called Ranikhet Express runs from New Delhi & Kathgodam.

NT6#0.quote: You can take a bus from Delhi kashmiri Gate ISBT and cover this journey in 7 hours approx.

NT7#0.quote: Built by the Britishers to connect the two ends of Nainital city, Mallital and Tallital, the iconic Mall Road is a must on most tourist's to-do list in Nainital.

NT7#1.quote: The must-buys here are handmade candles and pinewood artifacts crafted by local artisans.

NT8#0.quote: Plying between Snow View point and Mallital, the 3-minute one-way journey offers breathtaking aerial views of Nainital and Naini Lake.

NT8#1.quote: The charges are INR 300 per adult (two-way trip) and INR 200 for children up-to 12 years of age. It runs from 10 am every day

NT9#0.quote: the Snow View Point, located at 2,270 m above the sea level, offers stunning views of the snow-covered mountain peaks of the Great Himalayas.

NT9#1.quote: A large pair of binoculars is installed here to let visitors take a closer look at the peaks.

NT10#0.quote: The sacred Naina Devi temple with Goddess Naina Devi as its presiding deity is located atop the Naina hill near the Naini Lake.

NT10#1.quote: The Naina Peak, locally known as Cheena peak, is the highest point in Nainital.

NT11#0.quote: According to mythology, the lake is believed to have been formed when the eyes of goddess “Sati” fell at this spot

NT12#0.quote: A popular picnic spot in Nainital, Tiffin Top (also known as Dorothy's Seat) is located on Ayarpatta hill, and offers a panoramic view of the Nainital town and surrounding hills.

NT12#1.quote: many tourists also like to trek up to the place, which is just 4 km away from the town.

NT13#0.quote: the zoo is perched on the Sher Ka Danda hill at an altitude of 2,100 m above sea level. Spread over a green area of 4.6 hectare, the zoo is home to a variety of animals like the royal Bengal tiger, Tibetan wolves, leopard, various types of deer, and the Himalayan bear.

NT14#0.quote: On the Nainital to Almora Road, 9 km from Bhowali and 17 km from Nainital is the popular pilgrimage centre Kainchi Dham, a Hanuman Temple and ashram founded by the sage Neem Karoli Baba, in 1962.

NT15#0.quote: The place gained more recognition owing to a visit by Apple founder Steve Jobs, and the founder and CEO of Facebook Mark Zuckerberg.

NT16#0.quote: Pangot is a small picturesque hamlet famous for its jungles and birds, located just 15 km from Nainital.

NT16#1.quote: The Pangot and Kilbury Bird Sanctuary here is home to around 600 species of birds.

NT17#0.quote: Built in 1846, the beautiful church with Neo-Gothic architecture, stands in the middle of a forest, surrounded by tall deodar and pine trees.

NT18#0.quote: The Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences or ARIES is an observatory sitting on the Manora Peak in Nainital.

NT18#1.quote: It is also open to visitors.

NT19#0.quote: Opening Time:- 10.30 AM – 1 PM & 1.30 PM- 4 PMIs closed on Sunday and public holidays

NT20#0.quote: At a distance of 5 km from Nainital, Sariyatal is an almost heart-shaped lake located on Kaladungi Road in Nainital district.

NT20#1.quote: the emerald blue-green lake of Khurpatal is just 12 km away from Nainital.

NT20#2.quote: Situated at a distance of just 25 km from Nainital, the crystal-clear Naukuchiatal lake with its nine corners is a captivating sight.

NT21#0.quote: The Naini Lake offers several water sports options, including kayaking, canoeing, yachting and boating. Kayaking and paddle boating are the two most popular activities here.

NT22#0.quote: The trek starts at Mallital in Nainital and goes through the famous Snow View hill to reach Naini Peak (also known as Cheena Peak).

NT22#1.quote: Another popular and easy route is the Nainital to Khurpa Tal Trek, a walk of around 6.7 km.

NT23#0.quote: Famous for the temple of Lord Golu, the presiding local deity, and an Army School, Ghorakhal is at a distance of 17 km from Nainital.

NT24#0.quote: Mallital, the upper end of the Naini Lake and the Mall Road ,offers great shopping and dining options.

NT25#0.quote: The KMVN TRH Snow View guesthouse, which was once a Britisher's bungalow, is an excellent place to stay.

NT26#0.quote: Enjoy paragliding in and around Nainital, especially on the Bhimtal-Jangli Gaon road and Kotabagh.

NT26#1.quote: Hot-air ballooning camps are setup in and around Nainital, mainly at Sukhatal.
